name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q01 - Classical concepts of oxidation and reduction reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II according to the classical definitions of oxidation and reduction processes:

List-I (Chemical Reaction) List-II (Classical Definition)
A. \(2\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MgO}(\mathrm{s})\) I. Removal of oxygen from a compound
B. \(2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\) II. Addition of hydrogen to an unsaturated compound
C. \(2\mathrm{HgO}(\mathrm{s}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\mathrm{Hg}(\mathrm{l}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\) III. Addition of oxygen to an element
D. \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}_3(\mathrm{g})\) IV. Removal of hydrogen from a substance

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction of magnesium with oxygen
In the reaction \(2\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MgO}(\mathrm{s})\), elemental oxygen combines directly with metallic magnesium. By the classical definition, the addition of oxygen to an element constitutes oxidation.

Step 2: Reaction of hydrogen sulfide with oxygen
In the reaction \(2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{S}(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\), hydrogen is removed from hydrogen sulfide to produce solid sulfur. The classical definition defines the removal of hydrogen from a substance as an oxidation process.

Step 3: Thermal decomposition of mercuric oxide
In the reaction \(2\mathrm{HgO}(\mathrm{s}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\mathrm{Hg}(\mathrm{l}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\), oxygen is removed from mercuric oxide yielding liquid mercury. The classical definition classifies the removal of oxygen from a compound as reduction.

Step 4: Hydrogenation of ethene
In the reaction \(\mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}_3(\mathrm{g})\), dihydrogen is added across the double bond of ethene to form ethane. The classical definition defines the addition of hydrogen to a substance as reduction.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Combining the individual classical interpretations gives:
• Reaction of magnesium with oxygen corresponds to addition of oxygen to an element.
• Reaction of hydrogen sulfide with oxygen corresponds to removal of hydrogen from a substance.
• Thermal decomposition of mercuric oxide corresponds to removal of oxygen from a compound.
• Hydrogenation of ethene corresponds to addition of hydrogen to an unsaturated compound.
The correct combination is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q02 - Stock notation representation of metal compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II to represent the chemical compounds using Stock notation:

List-I (Compound Formula) List-II (Stock Notation Representation)
A. \(\mathrm{HAuCl}_4\) I. \(\mathrm{Tl}_2(\mathrm{I})\mathrm{O}\)
B. \(\mathrm{Tl}_2\mathrm{O}\) II. \(\mathrm{Fe}_2(\mathrm{III})\mathrm{O}_3\)
C. \(\mathrm{MnO}_2\) III. \(\mathrm{HAu}(\mathrm{III})\mathrm{Cl}_4\)
D. \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) IV. \(\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{IV})\mathrm{O}_2\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Oxidation state of gold in chloroauric acid
In \(\mathrm{HAuCl}_4\), hydrogen has an oxidation number of \(+1\) and chlorine has an oxidation number of \(-1\). Setting the sum of oxidation numbers equal to zero:
\(+1 + x + 4(-1) = 0 \implies x - 3 = 0 \implies x = +3\).
Thus, gold is present in the \(+3\) oxidation state, represented in Stock notation as \(\mathrm{HAu}(\mathrm{III})\mathrm{Cl}_4\).

Step 2: Oxidation state of thallium in thallous oxide
In \(\mathrm{Tl}_2\mathrm{O}\), oxygen has an oxidation number of \(-2\). For the neutral compound:
\(2x + (-2) = 0 \implies 2x = 2 \implies x = +1\).
Thus, thallium has an oxidation state of \(+1\), represented in Stock notation as \(\mathrm{Tl}_2(\mathrm{I})\mathrm{O}\).

Step 3: Oxidation state of manganese in manganese dioxide
In \(\mathrm{MnO}_2\), each oxygen atom has an oxidation number of \(-2\). For the neutral compound:
\(x + 2(-2) = 0 \implies x - 4 = 0 \implies x = +4\).
Thus, manganese is in the \(+4\) oxidation state, represented in Stock notation as \(\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{IV})\mathrm{O}_2\).

Step 4: Oxidation state of iron in ferric oxide
In \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\), each oxygen atom is assigned an oxidation state of \(-2\). Setting up the sum:
\(2x + 3(-2) = 0 \implies 2x - 6 = 0 \implies x = +3\).
Thus, iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state, represented in Stock notation as \(\mathrm{Fe}_2(\mathrm{III})\mathrm{O}_3\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The respective Stock representations are:
• \(\mathrm{HAuCl}_4\) corresponds to \(\mathrm{HAu}(\mathrm{III})\mathrm{Cl}_4\).
• \(\mathrm{Tl}_2\mathrm{O}\) corresponds to \(\mathrm{Tl}_2(\mathrm{I})\mathrm{O}\).
• \(\mathrm{MnO}_2\) corresponds to \(\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{IV})\mathrm{O}_2\).
• \(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\) corresponds to \(\mathrm{Fe}_2(\mathrm{III})\mathrm{O}_3\).
The correct combination is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q03 - Classification of different types of redox reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II to classify each redox reaction under its appropriate category:

List-I (Chemical Reaction) List-II (Type of Redox Reaction)
A. \(3\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{Mg}_3\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{s})\) I. Decomposition redox reaction
B. \(2\mathrm{KClO}_3(\mathrm{s}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\mathrm{KCl}(\mathrm{s}) + 3\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\) II. Combination redox reaction
C. \(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{s})\) III. Disproportionation redox reaction
D. \(\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{OH}^-(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{Cl}^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\) IV. Metal displacement redox reaction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reaction between magnesium and nitrogen
In the reaction \(3\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}_3\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{s})\), two elements in their uncombined states (oxidation states of zero) combine to form a single compound in which magnesium is \(+2\) and nitrogen is \(-3\). This fits the definition of a combination redox reaction.

Step 2: Thermal breakdown of potassium chlorate
In \(2\mathrm{KClO}_3(\mathrm{s}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl}(\mathrm{s}) + 3\mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g})\), potassium chlorate breaks down into two substances, one of which is the elemental gas \(\mathrm{O}_2\). The oxidation state of chlorine changes from \(+5\) to \(-1\) and that of oxygen changes from \(-2\) to \(0\). This represents a decomposition redox reaction.

Step 3: Reduction of chromium oxide by aluminium
In \(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{s}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{s}) + 2\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{s})\), uncombined aluminium displaces chromium metal from its oxide ore. Aluminium acts as a reducing metal because it is more reactive and easily loses electrons compared to chromium. This is a metal displacement redox reaction.

Step 4: Reaction of chlorine with cold dilute alkali
In \(\mathrm{Cl}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{OH}^-(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{Cl}^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\), chlorine in the zero oxidation state is simultaneously oxidised to \(+1\) in \(\mathrm{ClO}^-\) and reduced to \(-1\) in \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\). Since the same element experiences both oxidation and reduction from an intermediate state, this is a disproportionation redox reaction.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct reaction classifications are:
• Reaction of magnesium with nitrogen is a combination redox reaction.
• Decomposition of potassium chlorate is a decomposition redox reaction.
• Reduction of chromium(III) oxide by aluminium is a metal displacement redox reaction.
• Reaction of chlorine with hydroxide is a disproportionation redox reaction.
The correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q04 - Oxidation states of elements in various compounds

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II to identify the oxidation state of the underlined atom in each given species:

List-I (Chemical Species) List-II (Oxidation State of Underlined Element)
A. \(\mathrm{K}_2\underline{\mathrm{Mn}}\mathrm{O}_4\) I. \(+3\)
B. \(\mathrm{Na}\underline{\mathrm{B}}\mathrm{H}_4\) II. \(+6\)
C. \(\underline{\mathrm{O}}\mathrm{F}_2\) III. \(-1\)
D. \(\mathrm{Ca}\underline{\mathrm{O}}_2\) IV. \(+2\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Oxidation state of manganese in potassium manganate
In \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{MnO}_4\), each potassium atom exhibits an oxidation state of \(+1\) and each oxygen atom exhibits \(-2\). For the neutral molecule:
\(2(+1) + x + 4(-2) = 0 \implies 2 + x - 8 = 0 \implies x = +6\).
Thus, manganese has an oxidation state of \(+6\).

Step 2: Oxidation state of boron in sodium borohydride
In \(\mathrm{NaBH}_4\), sodium has an oxidation number of \(+1\). In the tetrahydroborate anion \(\mathrm{BH}_4^-\), hydrogen is bonded to the less electronegative element boron and behaves as hydride with an oxidation state of \(-1\). Setting the algebraic sum:
\(+1 + x + 4(-1) = 0 \implies x - 3 = 0 \implies x = +3\).
Thus, boron has an oxidation state of \(+3\).

Step 3: Oxidation state of oxygen in oxygen difluoride
In \(\mathrm{OF}_2\), fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table and strictly exhibits an oxidation number of \(-1\) in all its compounds. For the neutral molecule:
\(x + 2(-1) = 0 \implies x - 2 = 0 \implies x = +2\).
Thus, oxygen has an oxidation state of \(+2\).

Step 4: Oxidation state of oxygen in calcium peroxide
In \(\mathrm{CaO}_2\), calcium is an alkaline earth metal that always possesses an oxidation state of \(+2\) in its compounds. For the neutral compound containing peroxide linkage:
\(+2 + 2x = 0 \implies 2x = -2 \implies x = -1\).
Thus, oxygen exhibits an oxidation state of \(-1\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The assigned oxidation numbers are:
• Manganese in potassium manganate has an oxidation state of \(+6\).
• Boron in sodium borohydride has an oxidation state of \(+3\).
• Oxygen in oxygen difluoride has an oxidation state of \(+2\).
• Oxygen in calcium peroxide has an oxidation state of \(-1\).
The correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q05 - Average oxidation numbers from fractional paradox structures

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II to match each chemical species with the average oxidation state of its key constituent element:

List-I (Chemical Species) List-II (Average Oxidation Number)
A. Carbon suboxide (\(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{O}_2\)) I. \(+\frac{16}{3}\)
B. Tribromooctaoxide (\(\mathrm{Br}_3\mathrm{O}_8\)) II. \(+2.5\)
C. Tetrathionate ion (\(\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-}\)) III. \(-\frac{1}{2}\)
D. Potassium superoxide (\(\mathrm{KO}_2\)) IV. \(+\frac{4}{3}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Average oxidation number of carbon in carbon suboxide
In \(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{O}_2\), oxygen has an oxidation state of \(-2\). For the neutral compound:
\(3x + 2(-2) = 0 \implies 3x - 4 = 0 \implies x = +\frac{4}{3}\).
Thus, the average oxidation number of carbon is \(+\frac{4}{3}\).

Step 2: Average oxidation number of bromine in tribromooctaoxide
In \(\mathrm{Br}_3\mathrm{O}_8\), each oxygen atom has an assigned oxidation state of \(-2\). For the neutral oxide:
\(3x + 8(-2) = 0 \implies 3x - 16 = 0 \implies x = +\frac{16}{3}\).
Thus, the average oxidation number of bromine is \(+\frac{16}{3}\).

Step 3: Average oxidation number of sulfur in tetrathionate
In the polyatomic ion \(\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-}\), each oxygen atom has an oxidation number of \(-2\). Equating the algebraic sum of oxidation numbers to the overall charge \(-2\):
\(4x + 6(-2) = -2 \implies 4x - 12 = -2 \implies 4x = +10 \implies x = +2.5\).
Thus, the average oxidation number of sulfur is \(+2.5\).

Step 4: Average oxidation number of oxygen in potassium superoxide
In \(\mathrm{KO}_2\), potassium is an alkali metal with a fixed oxidation number of \(+1\). In the superoxide ion \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\):
\(+1 + 2x = 0 \implies 2x = -1 \implies x = -\frac{1}{2}\).
Thus, the average oxidation number of oxygen is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The average oxidation numbers for each species are:
• Carbon in carbon suboxide has an average oxidation state of \(+\frac{4}{3}\).
• Bromine in tribromooctaoxide has an average oxidation state of \(+\frac{16}{3}\).
• Sulfur in tetrathionate ion has an average oxidation state of \(+2.5\).
• Oxygen in potassium superoxide has an average oxidation state of \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
The correct combination is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q06 - Stoichiometric coefficients of water in balanced equations

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II to match each redox reaction with the coefficient and location of water (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\)) in its balanced net ionic equation:

List-I (Redox Reaction System) List-II (Coefficient and Position of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\))
A. Oxidation of \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) by \(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\) in acidic medium I. \(1\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the reactant side
B. Oxidation of \(\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\) by \(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\) in acidic medium II. \(4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the reactant side
C. Oxidation of \(\mathrm{Br}^{-}\) by \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}\) in basic medium III. \(7\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the product side
D. Oxidation of \(\mathrm{I}^{-}\) by \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}\) in basic medium to form \(\mathrm{I}_2\) and \(\mathrm{MnO}_2\) IV. \(4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the product side

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Dichromate oxidation of ferrous ion in acidic medium
The balanced reduction half-reaction is:
\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}(\mathrm{aq}) + 14\mathrm{H}^+(\mathrm{aq}) + 6\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 7\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\).
The oxidation half-reaction is \(6\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 6\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 6\mathrm{e}^-\).
Summing the half-reactions gives the overall balanced equation:
\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}(\mathrm{aq}) + 6\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 14\mathrm{H}^+(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 6\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 7\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\).
This contains \(7\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the product side.

Step 2: Dichromate oxidation of sulfite ion in acidic medium
The oxidation state of chromium decreases from \(+6\) to \(+3\) (\(\Delta = -3\) per Cr, total decrease of \(6\)). The oxidation state of sulfur increases from \(+4\) to \(+6\) (\(\Delta = +2\)). To equalize electron transfer, 3 sulfite ions react per dichromate ion:
\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}(\mathrm{aq}) + 3\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}(\mathrm{aq}) + 8\mathrm{H}^+(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 3\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-}(\mathrm{aq}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\).
This contains \(4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the product side.

Step 3: Permanganate oxidation of bromide ion in basic medium
Permanganate is reduced from \(+7\) to \(+4\) (\(\mathrm{MnO}_2\), decrease of \(3\)). Bromide is oxidised from \(-1\) to \(+5\) in bromate (\(\mathrm{BrO}_3^-\), increase of \(6\)). Balancing changes gives a mole ratio of \(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) to \(1\mathrm{Br}^-\):
\(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{Br}^-(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}_2(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{BrO}_3^-(\mathrm{aq}) + 2\mathrm{OH}^-(\mathrm{aq})\).
This contains \(1\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the reactant side.

Step 4: Permanganate oxidation of iodide ion in basic medium
The balanced half-reactions in basic medium are:
\(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^-(\mathrm{aq}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) + 6\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 8\mathrm{OH}^-(\mathrm{aq})\)
and \(6\mathrm{I}^-(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 3\mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 6\mathrm{e}^-\).
Adding these yields the balanced equation:
\(2\mathrm{MnO}_4^-(\mathrm{aq}) + 6\mathrm{I}^-(\mathrm{aq}) + 4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MnO}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 3\mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{s}) + 8\mathrm{OH}^-(\mathrm{aq})\).
This contains \(4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the reactant side.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The stoichiometric coefficients and positions of water are:
• Oxidation of \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) by \(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\) in acid has \(7\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the product side.
• Oxidation of \(\mathrm{SO}_3^{2-}\) by \(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\) in acid has \(4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the product side.
• Oxidation of \(\mathrm{Br}^-\) by \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) in base has \(1\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the reactant side.
• Oxidation of \(\mathrm{I}^-\) by \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) in base has \(4\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) on the reactant side.
The correct combination is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q07 - Indicators and observation in redox titration methods

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the indicator principles and visual observations in redox titrations:

List-I (Titration / Reaction System) List-II (Indicator Mechanism / Visual End Point)
A. Permanganate titration against \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) or \(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{O}_4^{2-}\) I. Starch indicator gives an intense blue colour that disappears once iodine is fully consumed
B. Dichromate titration against \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) in acidic medium II. Reagent acts as self-indicator; first lasting pink tinge appears at equivalence point
C. Iodometric titration of liberated \(\mathrm{I}_2\) with \(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\) III. Diphenylamine is oxidised just after equivalence point to produce an intense blue colour
D. Reaction of \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}\) ions with excess iodide ions IV. Iodine is liberated quantitatively along with the formation of cuprous iodide (\(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{I}_2\)) precipitate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Permanganate as a self-indicator
In permanganate titrations, \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) is intensely coloured. Once the reducing agent (\(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) or oxalate) is completely oxidized, the very first excess drop of \(\mathrm{MnO}_4^-\) imparts a lasting pale pink colour at concentrations as low as \(10^{-6}\mathrm{\ mol\ dm}^{-3}\). Hence, it acts as a self-indicator.

Step 2: Dichromate indicator mechanism
Potassium dichromate (\(\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_7^{2-}\)) is not a self-indicator because its reduction product \(\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}\) is green, masking subtle colour shifts. It requires an external redox-sensitive indicator such as diphenylamine, which is oxidized by the first slight excess of dichromate immediately after the equivalence point to produce an intense blue colour.

Step 3: Iodometric titration with thiosulfate
In titrations involving free iodine and sodium thiosulfate (\(\mathrm{S}_2\mathrm{O}_3^{2-}\)), starch is added as a specific indicator. Starch forms an intense deep-blue adsorption complex with molecular iodine (\(\mathrm{I}_3^-\)). At the end point, the reduction of iodine to iodide causes the sudden and complete disappearance of the blue colour.

Step 4: Oxidation of iodide by cupric ions
When copper(II) ions react with excess iodide ions, copper(II) is reduced to copper(I), precipitating insoluble white cuprous iodide (\(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{I}_2\)), while iodide is oxidised to molecular iodine via the reaction:
\(2\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 4\mathrm{I}^-(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{aq})\).
The liberated iodine can subsequently be titrated against standard thiosulfate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct indicator correspondences are:
• Permanganate titration corresponds to self-indicator action with a lasting pink tinge.
• Dichromate titration corresponds to diphenylamine producing an intense blue colour at the end point.
• Iodometric titration corresponds to starch giving an intense blue colour that disappears when iodine is reduced.
• Reaction of copper(II) with iodide corresponds to formation of \(\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{I}_2\) precipitate and liberation of \(\mathrm{I}_2\).
The correct combination is A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q08 - Disproportionation behavior of chlorine oxoanions species

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II to correlate the oxoanions of chlorine with their characteristic disproportionation pathways:

List-I (Chlorine Oxoanion) List-II (Disproportionation Characteristics)
A. \(\mathrm{ClO}^-\) I. Disproportionates to yield \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) and \(\mathrm{ClO}_4^-\)
B. \(\mathrm{ClO}_2^-\) II. Does not disproportionate because chlorine is in its maximum group oxidation state (\(+7\))
C. \(\mathrm{ClO}_3^-\) III. Disproportionates to yield \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\) and \(\mathrm{ClO}_3^-\)
D. \(\mathrm{ClO}_4^-\) IV. Photochemically disproportionates to yield \(\mathrm{ClO}_3^-\) and \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Disproportionation of hypochlorite ion
In the hypochlorite ion (\(\mathrm{ClO}^-\)), chlorine is in the \(+1\) oxidation state. It readily disproportionates according to the reaction:
\(3\mathrm{ClO}^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cl}^- + \mathrm{ClO}_3^-\).
Chlorine experiences both reduction to \(-1\) in chloride and oxidation to \(+5\) in chlorate.

Step 2: Disproportionation of chlorite ion
In the chlorite ion (\(\mathrm{ClO}_2^-\)), chlorine exhibits an oxidation state of \(+3\). Under photochemical excitation (\(h\nu\)), it disproportionates as:
\(6\mathrm{ClO}_2^- \xrightarrow{h\nu} 4\mathrm{ClO}_3^- + 2\mathrm{Cl}^-\).
Chlorine increases its oxidation state from \(+3\) to \(+5\) in chlorate and decreases to \(-1\) in chloride.

Step 3: Disproportionation of chlorate ion
In the chlorate ion (\(\mathrm{ClO}_3^-\)), chlorine exhibits an oxidation state of \(+5\). Upon heating or disproportionation, it follows the reaction:
\(4\mathrm{ClO}_3^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Cl}^- + 3\mathrm{ClO}_4^-\).
Chlorine decreases its oxidation state from \(+5\) to \(-1\) in chloride and increases to \(+7\) in perchlorate.

Step 4: Non-disproportionation of perchlorate ion
In the perchlorate ion (\(\mathrm{ClO}_4^-\)), chlorine is in its highest possible group oxidation state of \(+7\) (since group number is 17, maximum oxidation state is \(17 - 10 = +7\)). For an element to undergo disproportionation, it must exist in an intermediate oxidation state and be capable of forming both higher and lower oxidation states. Because chlorine cannot increase its oxidation number beyond \(+7\), perchlorate cannot disproportionate.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The behavior of the chlorine oxoanions matches as follows:
• Hypochlorite disproportionates to yield chloride and chlorate.
• Chlorite photochemically disproportionates to yield chlorate and chloride.
• Chlorate disproportionates to yield chloride and perchlorate.
• Perchlorate does not disproportionate because chlorine is in its maximum oxidation state of \(+7\).
The correct combination is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q09 - Structural oxidation states of fractional paradox species

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II to correlate compounds displaying fractional average oxidation numbers with their actual constituent structural oxidation states:

List-I (Chemical Compound) List-II (Individual Structural Oxidation States)
A. Carbon suboxide (\(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{O}_2\)) I. Two terminal atoms each at \(+6\) and one central atom at \(+4\)
B. Tribromooctaoxide (\(\mathrm{Br}_3\mathrm{O}_8\)) II. Stoichiometric mixed oxide composed of one metal ion at \(+2\) and two metal ions at \(+3\)
C. Tetrathionate ion (\(\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-}\)) III. Two terminal atoms each at \(+2\) and one central atom at \(0\)
D. Ferrosoferric oxide (\(\mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm{O}_4\)) IV. Two terminal atoms each at \(+5\) and two central atoms each at \(0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural oxidation states in carbon suboxide
The Lewis structure of carbon suboxide is \(\mathrm{O}=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}^*=\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\). Each of the two terminal carbon atoms is bonded to a more electronegative oxygen atom via a double bond and to a carbon atom via a double bond, giving them each an oxidation state of \(+2\). The central carbon atom is bonded exclusively to two identical carbon atoms, giving it an oxidation state of \(0\). The average is \(\frac{+2 + 0 + 2}{3} = +\frac{4}{3}\).

Step 2: Structural oxidation states in tribromooctaoxide
In \(\mathrm{Br}_3\mathrm{O}_8\), the structure has three linearly linked bromine atoms: \(\mathrm{O}_3\mathrm{Br}-\mathrm{BrO}_2-\mathrm{BrO}_3\). Each of the two terminal bromine atoms is bonded to three oxygen atoms, which assigns them an oxidation state of \(+6\) each. The central bromine atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms and two bromine atoms, giving it an oxidation state of \(+4\). The average is \(\frac{+6 + 4 + 6}{3} = +\frac{16}{3}\).

Step 3: Structural oxidation states in tetrathionate ion
In \(\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6^{2-}\), the structure consists of a sulfur chain: \([^{-}O_3\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{S}^*-\mathrm{S}^*-\mathrm{SO}_3^-]\). The two terminal sulfur atoms are bonded to three oxygen atoms each, placing them in the \(+5\) oxidation state. The two central sulfur atoms participate only in homonuclear sulfur-sulfur bonds, giving each of them an oxidation state of \(0\). The average is \(\frac{+5 + 0 + 0 + 5}{4} = +2.5\).

Step 4: Stoichiometric composition of ferrosoferric oxide
The mixed oxide \(\mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm{O}_4\) has an apparent fractional average oxidation state of \(+\frac{8}{3}\). In reality, it is a stoichiometric mixed crystal composed of one mole of ferrous oxide (\(\mathrm{FeO}\)) and one mole of ferric oxide (\(\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3\)). Consequently, one iron atom is present as \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) (oxidation state \(+2\)) and two iron atoms are present as \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) (oxidation state \(+3\)).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The structural assignments correspond as follows:
• Carbon suboxide consists of two terminal atoms at \(+2\) and one central atom at \(0\).
• Tribromooctaoxide consists of two terminal atoms at \(+6\) and one central atom at \(+4\).
• Tetrathionate ion consists of two terminal atoms at \(+5\) and two central atoms at \(0\).
• Ferrosoferric oxide consists of one iron atom at \(+2\) and two iron atoms at \(+3\).
The correct combination is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_REDOXREACTIONS_MCQ_Q10 - Standard reduction potentials and feasibility of reactions

questiontext.text:
Given standard reduction potentials at \(298\mathrm{\ K}\):
\(\mathrm{E}^\circ(\mathrm{F}_2/\mathrm{F}^-) = +2.87\mathrm{\ V}\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ(\mathrm{Ag}^+/\mathrm{Ag}) = +0.80\mathrm{\ V}\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}) = +0.77\mathrm{\ V}\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ(\mathrm{I}_2/\mathrm{I}^-) = +0.54\mathrm{\ V}\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}) = +0.34\mathrm{\ V}\), and \(\mathrm{E}^\circ(\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}/\mathrm{Zn}) = -0.76\mathrm{\ V}\).
Match List-I with List-II regarding the electrochemical characteristics and thermodynamic feasibility of the processes:

List-I (Redox System / Process) List-II (Potential and Feasibility at \(298\mathrm{\ K}\))
A. Reaction between \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq})\) and \(\mathrm{I}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})\) I. Non-feasible because standard cell potential is negative (\(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -0.03\mathrm{\ V}\))
B. Reaction between \(\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})\) and \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq})\) II. Feasible and spontaneous because \(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.23\mathrm{\ V} > 0\)
C. Reaction between \(\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{s})\) and \(\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})\) in Daniell cell III. Possesses the highest positive reduction potential (\(+2.87\mathrm{\ V}\)), making it the strongest oxidant
D. Half-reaction: \(\mathrm{F}_2(\mathrm{g}) + 2\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow 2\mathrm{F}^-(\mathrm{aq})\) IV. Highly spontaneous reaction with standard cell potential \(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +1.10\mathrm{\ V}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Feasibility of reaction between ferric ion and iodide
The proposed reaction is \(2\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 2\mathrm{I}^-(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{I}_2(\mathrm{s})\).
Cathode (reduction): \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + \mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ = +0.77\mathrm{\ V}\).
Anode (oxidation): \(2\mathrm{I}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{I}_2 + 2\mathrm{e}^-\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ = +0.54\mathrm{\ V}\).
\(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = \mathrm{E}^\circ(\text{cathode}) - \mathrm{E}^\circ(\text{anode}) = +0.77\mathrm{\ V} - 0.54\mathrm{\ V} = +0.23\mathrm{\ V}\).
Because \(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} > 0\), \(\Delta G^\circ = -nF\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} < 0\), the reaction is spontaneous and feasible under standard conditions.

Step 2: Feasibility of reaction between metallic silver and ferric ion
The proposed reaction is \(\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Ag}^+(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq})\).
Cathode (reduction): \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+} + \mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ = +0.77\mathrm{\ V}\).
Anode (oxidation): \(\mathrm{Ag} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ag}^+ + \mathrm{e}^-\), \(\mathrm{E}^\circ = +0.80\mathrm{\ V}\).
\(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.77\mathrm{\ V} - 0.80\mathrm{\ V} = -0.03\mathrm{\ V}\).
Because \(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} < 0\), the reaction cannot proceed spontaneously under standard conditions.

Step 3: Daniell cell reaction
For the reaction \(\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{s})\):
Cathode (reduction of copper): \(\mathrm{E}^\circ = +0.34\mathrm{\ V}\).
Anode (oxidation of zinc): \(\mathrm{E}^\circ = -0.76\mathrm{\ V}\).
\(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.34\mathrm{\ V} - (-0.76\mathrm{\ V}) = +1.10\mathrm{\ V}\).
This represents a highly spontaneous galvanic cell reaction.

Step 4: Oxidising capability of elemental fluorine
The standard electrode potential of the \(\mathrm{F}_2/\mathrm{F}^-\) couple is \(+2.87\mathrm{\ V}\), which is the highest positive value in the electrochemical series. A higher positive reduction potential indicates a maximum tendency of the oxidised form to accept electrons and be reduced, making \(\mathrm{F}_2\) the strongest oxidising agent listed.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The electrochemical features match as follows:
• Reaction of \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) with \(\mathrm{I}^-\) is feasible with \(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = +0.23\mathrm{\ V}\).
• Reaction of \(\mathrm{Ag}\) with \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) is non-feasible with \(\mathrm{E}^\circ_{\text{cell}} = -0.03\mathrm{\ V}\).
• Daniell cell reaction produces a cell potential of \(+1.10\mathrm{\ V}\).
• Reduction of \(\mathrm{F}_2\) possesses \(\mathrm{E}^\circ = +2.87\mathrm{\ V}\), acting as the strongest oxidizing couple.
The correct combination is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.
